newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks stumble to sharply lower close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks stumble to sharply lower close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks fell to a sharply lower close on Monday, prompted by a drop on Wall Street and weakness in the local property market, brokers said.
"It (market weakness) is due to a combination of concerns about the property market and Wall Street," said Janet Gillies, sales director at OCBC Securities.
The Hang Seng Index closed 220.63 points, or 1.76 percent, lower at 12,295.97, after clawing back some ground from a low of 12,264.76.
Turnover was a respectable HK$7.64 billion, but well down from Friday's HK$9.33 billion.
The Dow Industrials fell 148.36 points, or 2.27 percent, to close at 6,391.69, following the release of a much higher than forecast rise in U.S. wholesale prices in March.
Brokers and investors said the data signalled a rise in U.S. inflation and may point to further hikes in interest rates.

Property also weighed on sentiment. Over the weekend Swire Properties Ltd offered more units in its upmarket Island Place development, but interest in this batch was significantly lower than that for previous sales programmes, brokers said. The 13 percent rise in the average sales prices was thought to be the chief negative factor.
Government move to cool pricea and higher interest rates have also been blamed for slowing demand in the property market.
Swire Properties is a division of conglomerate Swire Pacific Ltd. The share closed HK$0.50 lower at HK$59.75.
The property sector led the market down followed by finance counters.
Developers Henderson Land ended the day HK$1.50 lower at HK$62.75. Sun Hung Kai Properties also dropped HK$1.50 to a HK$76.25 close.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings shed HK$3.50 to HK$180.50. The market's most liquid counter was also the most vulnerable to profit-taking pressures, brokers said.
Red chips and H shares remained resilient. China Resources rose to a year high of HK$18.50, then eased to close HK$0.45 higher at HK$18.40.
Tsingtao Brewery put on HK$0.075 to close at HK$3.50.
Technically speaking, the market has good support at 12,000 level, its 250-day moving average.
"Selling pressure is not that high," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities. "Turnover dropped off again on the market's downturn."
Major support lies at 11,500, Shum said.
